headline: Computational methods infer cell-cell and proximity effects from spatial transcriptomics
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Computational Inference
summary: Spatial transcriptomics tools now model proximity effects, predict missing modalities, and benchmark cell-cell communication inference.
synthesis: The common thread is computational inference of structure that sequencing alone does not resolve, applied to spatial transcriptomic data. PACE separates cell-type-resolved proximity effects on gene expression, SPARKLE corrects local RNA leakage in Stereo-seq and Visium HD, and SPADE flags spatially aberrant epithelial spots using conformal prediction. Other items extend coverage across modalities or sample structure: SpatialMOC predicts missing spatial molecular layers, SPCC maps unpaired single-cell profiles onto spatial data, and spHOT localizes phenotype-associated spatial biomarkers from sample-level labels. CIFM forward-simulates tissue transcriptional dynamics to support perturbation design, and CoxFormer provides 512-dimensional embeddings for 32,016 human genes. A review of 33 cell-cell communication methods and a benchmark of four annotation methods on 45 NSCLC Visium samples, where CARD and RCTD were most concordant, show the field now evaluating these tools against one another. The tissue division-of-labor and tumor clonal ecology items address biology more than method.
